The proposed answer is incorrect. The solution substitutes u = p(v) but drops the factor du = p'(v) dv.

Correct computation: with p(x) = x⁷ + 6x⁵ + 3x³ + 1, we have p(1) = 11 and p(−1) = −9, so the limits map to v = −1 and v = 1. Then

∫₋₉¹¹ f(u) du = ∫₋₁¹ (9v + 5) p'(v) dv.

- The 5 term gives 5·(p(1) − p(−1)) = 5·20 = 100.
- The 9v term, by parts, gives 9([v·p(v)]₋₁¹ − ∫₋₁¹ p(v) dv) = 9(2 − 2) = 0. Here [v·p(v)]₋₁¹ = 11 − 9 = 2, and ∫₋₁¹ p(v) dv = 2 because the odd terms integrate to zero and the constant 1 contributes 2.

The integral equals 100, not 10.
